ak_upper_pivot_point.blurb: A small, quiet roadside crag on the Seward Highway in south-central Alaska, tucked above the more visited Pivot Point wall. The seven lines here are short and friendly: a few bolted sport routes, a pair of top-ropes, one trad line and a single easy boulder problem. Grades stay moderate, mostly 5.6 through 5.9, which suits newer climbers and anyone wanting a relaxed warm-up. It is reached by taking the left branch of the path at Pivot Point and continuing uphill for roughly five minutes. The spot feels removed from the highway noise. Bugs can be thick depending on the year, and a black bear has been reported nosing around the upper area, so keep food stowed.

ak_marbless.blurb: Marbless is a small bouldering zone along Sheep Creek, in the Fairbanks region of interior Alaska. It holds seven problems that run from the mid-V3 range up into V6 or V7, so it is aimed at climbers with some experience rather than beginners. It is regarded locally as one of the nicest boulders in the Interior. Getting there takes a walk from the Nenana Bridge area: follow the railroad tracks south to the creek trestle and head into the creek, where it lies about five minutes upstream of the Midway boulders, or around 15 to 20 minutes from the trestle itself. Expect a quiet creekside setting with a short list of problems rather than a full circuit.

ak_freight_boulder.blurb: Freight Boulder is the first block you meet in Sheep Creek near Fairbanks, in interior Alaska, and you can see it from the railroad trestle. It carries seven problems, all on the easier side: a spread from V1 through V4, with most sitting around V2 and V3. The face climbing is described as decent, and the landings are good, which makes it a comfortable stop for newer boulderers or for warming up before other blocks in the creek. From the trestle it is only about 200 feet upstream. The trestle is reached by walking the railroad tracks south for roughly 15 minutes from the Nenana Bridge pull-off.
